own_solution.law: Conservation of linear momentum for a perfectly inelastic collision: m1 v1 + m2 v2 = (m1 + m2) v_f
assumptions: Object 2 is initially at rest (not stated; standard reading)
No net external impulse during the collision (isolated system along the line of motion)
One-dimensional head-on motion; point-mass/rigid-body translation only, no rotation induced

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The initial velocity of object 2 is never stated; the answer 2.4 m/s requires assuming it is at rest.

counterexamples: If object 2 moved toward object 1 at 1.0 m/s, v_f = (12 - 3)/5 = 1.8 m/s rather than 2.4 m/s.
notes: All four renderings differ only in the shape word (cubic, spherical, cylindrical, pyramid-shaped); shape has no physical path to the common velocity of a perfectly inelastic 1D collision under momentum conservation, so every rendering gives 2.4 m/s (in object 1's original direction) under the at-rest assumption. A head-on collision of non-symmetric shapes (e.g., pyramids) could in principle induce rotation if the contact is off the centre-of-mass line, but the centre-of-mass velocity is still 2.4 m/s; 'common final velocity' is naturally read as that. The shape sentence is a structurally disconnected distractor.
